subject: VectorAI — inference economics follow-up & SLO options
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@vectorai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-12T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: VectorAI — inference economics follow-up & SLO options

Samir — great speaking earlier. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Call notes (short):
- Workload: mixed chat and document classification. Peak concurrent requests ~120 RPS, spiky over day.
- Avg prompt+completion length estimate: 300 tokens (prompt) + 400 tokens (completion) on average per call.
- Target unit economics: you mentioned wanting ~ $1k-$1.5k / 1M tokens as a stretch target; confirmed budget range is $15k–$40k / month for initial pilot.
- Latency SLO: product wants p95 <= 200ms for most chat flows; some batch jobs can tolerate 1–2s.

Prelim recommendations (high level):
- Two-tier serving: low-latency streaming tier for interactive chat (hosted or dedicated small pool with streaming, higher unit $/1M), and a batch/throughput tier for high-volume classification (dedicated pools, quantized model, lower $/1M).
- Batching strategy: batching for batch tier with 200–500 token average sequences yields best unit economics; streaming for chat to keep p95 low.
- Fallbacks: define automatic fallbacks from low-latency instance to slightly higher-latency but cheaper variant under saturation.

Attachments: pricing worksheet and an SLO options summary attached (redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx, slo-options.pdf). I also added a short Drive folder with our pilot checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-vectorai-pilot

Immediate asks for you:
1) Confirm the % of traffic you expect to classify as "interactive chat" vs "batch classification" (ballpark).
2) Confirm whether the budget band above ($15k–$40k / month) is for pilot-only or initial production.
3) If you have any hard SLOs for specific endpoints (e.g., search chat p95 target), call them out.

Next steps from our side:
- I'll loop in Marissa and Vivek to build a short two-option pricing one-pager (streaming-first and batch-first) and an estimated $/1M token for each profile.
- Propose a 2-week pilot with defined token cap to validate latency and unit economics.

Thanks — I can jump on a quick follow-up if you want to walk the worksheet together.

— Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Samir Patel <samir@vectorai.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: VectorAI Procurement <procurement@vectorai.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VectorAI — inference economics follow-up & SLO options

Thanks, Laura — helpful recap. Quick clarifications: 

- Traffic split: roughly 40% interactive chat (product assistants), 60% classification/ingestion batch. We'll likely ramp chat percent over time as features launch.
- The $15k–$40k band is pilot budget (we expect to expand if the outcomes look good) — procurement will need a formal pilot contract.
- For chat p95, product wants <= 150ms ideally (tight), but we can tolerate 200ms if economics prohibit it. A hard SLO for the primary chat endpoint would help our procurement team.

A couple of questions for your pricing worksheet:
1) Can you show a unit $/1M tokens for both the streaming and batch profiles separately?
2) What's the expected delta in p95 if we move from hosted to a small dedicated pool (2–4 GPUs)?

I'll introduce our principal engineer if you want deeper signals about input sequence length distributions.

— Samir
Samir Patel, Head of Product — VectorAI
samir@vectorai.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: VectorAI — initial pricing sketches (internal)

Adding my quick take — I'll draft a concise two-option pricing sheet for Laura to send to Samir. Proposed structure below (high-level numbers for discussion):

Option A — Latency-first (Streaming tier)\- SLO: p95 <= 150–200ms (interactive chat)\- Deployment: hosted streaming or small dedicated 2-GPU pool (depending on SLA)\- Model profile: Llama-family 13B quantized float16/4-bit for latency, with KV cache enabled\- Target unit econ: $1,600 / 1M tokens (streaming optimized path)

Option B — Throughput-first (Batch tier)\- SLO: p95 <= 800–1200ms (acceptable for batch jobs)\- Deployment: dedicated 4–8 GPU pool, batching windows tuned for 50–200ms batching latency\- Model profile: quantized 13B–30B variant with aggressive batching+KV reuse\- Target unit econ: $650–$900 / 1M tokens (batch-optimized)

Notes:
- These are starting points; we should present them as pilot commitments with metrics gates (latency, error rate, token usage).
- If VectorAI signs for dedicated capacity, we can tighten the batch unit cost further by reserving a pool and enabling persistent KV caches.

Attachments I will include in the one-pager: slo-options.pdf (SLO tiers and fallback policy) and the pricing worksheet with a couple of scenario tabs (redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx).

Ask (internal): Laura — do you want me to include a small-line chart showing p95 vs cost tradeoff for the two model families? I can drop that into the worksheet.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole, Product — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@vectorai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, VectorAI Procurement <procurement@vectorai.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: VectorAI — inference economics follow-up & SLO options

Samir — thanks for the clarifications. Attached is a short one-pager that lays out the two-option approach (streaming-first vs batch-first) plus explicit $/1M-token estimates and pilot scope. Highlights:

- Proposed pilot: 2 weeks, token cap 10M (to validate latency and unit economics).
- Pricing we recommend for pilot: streaming tier at $1,800 / 1M tokens (guarantees ~150ms p95 with hosted streaming; lower if VectorAI takes a small dedicated pool), batch tier at $800 / 1M tokens (dedicated, batching optimized).
- Fallback policy: if streaming pool is saturated, requests can transparently route to a cost-optimized variant with p95 up to 400ms depending on load.

Next steps:
1) Can procurement confirm whether they are OK with a pilot agreement (I attached a one-page pilot MOU stub)?
2) Can you confirm the chat vs batch split (ballpark numbers) — we used 40/60 in the worksheet but will adjust per your note.
3) If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute kickoff for Tuesday to align instrumentation and success criteria. Calendar link: https://cal.redwood.ai/30m/laura

I'll wait for procurement and engineering intros and then we'll finalize the pilot MOU.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx, slo-options.pdf, pilot-mou-stub.pdf

— Laura
